Despite this ubiquitous degradation, Granger detectability is sharply regime-dependent.
The onset we report reflects PermG's statistical power curve crossing the detection threshold at a critical contamination level, not the emergence of a new physical signal; this interpretation is confirmed by sub-threshold $p$-values at $\alpha{=}0.45$ (\S\ref{sec:theory}).
Permutation Granger (PermG) tests find 0/8 canary$\to$downstream pairs FDR-significant from $\alpha{=}0.00$ through $\alpha{=}0.45$, then jump to 6/8 at $\alpha{=}0.50$ in 2 of 3~fp32 seeds (s42, s44: 6/8; s43: 0/8).
This transition is striking because cumulative synthetic fraction barely changes across the boundary: $C = 1{-}(1{-}\alpha)^{10}$ yields $99.75\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.45$ versus $99.90\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.50$, a difference of 0.15 percentage points, yet detection jumps from null to reliable.
Sigmoid regression on the 13-point $T{=}10$ grid yields $\alpha_c = 0.483 \pm 0.006$ ($R^2 = 0.969$); dense $\alpha$ sampling (17~values) constrains the onset steepness to $k{=}15.7$ (95\% CI $[9.4, 28.2]$), a steep but finite-width sigmoid (Figure~\ref{fig:regime_map}).
This single-$T$ estimate is consistent with the cross-$T$ validated model (\S\ref{sec:theory}), which predicts how the detection boundary shifts with observation length ($\gamma{=}2.08$).
The transition is not a literal step function ($\Delta\mathrm{AIC}{=}-110$ favoring sigmoid; Appendix~\ref{app:sigmoid_shape}), but its steepness (${\approx}3{\times}$ smooth-model predictions; \S\ref{sec:theory}) exceeds what PermG power curves alone produce.
At $T{=}10$, PermG power is ${\approx}37\%$ (Appendix~\ref{app:power_sim}), partly amplifying the $0/8{\to}6/8$ sharpness; however, onset steepness ($k{=}15.7$, ${\approx}3{\times}$ smooth predictions) and cross-seed consistency (2/3 seeds: $0/8{\to}6/8$ at $\alpha{=}0.48{\to}0.50$) argue for a genuine, power-modulated transition.
A Fisher exact test corroborates the categorical jump: 0/64 pairs FDR-significant at $\alpha \leq 0.45$ versus 18/32 at $\alpha \geq 0.50$ ($p = 3.45 \times 10^{-11}$); sub-threshold $p$-values at $\alpha{=}0.45$ ($p_{\mathrm{fdr}} = 0.059$--$0.091$) are consistent with proximity to the power boundary (\S\ref{sec:theory}).
A systematic robustness analysis (1{,}160 configurations) confirms specification-invariance of the onset.

First-differencing scopes the canary claim precisely.
Canary$\to$diversity pairs retain unanimous FDR significance after first-differencing ($24/24 \to 24/24$ across 4~seeds at $\alpha{=}1.0$, 6 pairs per seed), while canary$\to$perplexity collapses entirely ($F \approx 0$, $p = 0.99$): the apparent perplexity association is a shared-trend artifact.
All canary claims are therefore scoped to diversity metrics only.
This scoping reflects a genuine temporal structure difference, not selective power loss from differencing: $|r|$ retention is ${\geq}95\%$ for both channels, but canary$\to$diversity correlations peak at lagged offsets (81\% at lag${<}0$, median${=}-1$) while canary$\to$perplexity correlations are contemporaneous (50\% at lag${=}0$), producing $20$--$28{\times}$ lower Granger $F$ for perplexity (Appendix~\ref{app:channel_effect_size}; perplexity $n{=}8$, limited sample).

\section*{Limitations}
\label{sec:limitations}

Our landscape characterization uses Pythia-410M as the primary architecture; the phase diagram (\S\ref{sec:t20}) is Pythia-family-only (410M and 1.4B; Appendix~\ref{app:scale_14b}), not cross-architecture.
Cross-architecture validation spans five families (345M--6.9B) but five of fifteen conditions do not confirm unambiguous directional detection (including GPT-2-medium s43 fp32, which shows bidirectional Granger significance despite clean directionality at s42), and frontier-scale behavior ($>$7B) is untested.
At 1.4B, entropy saturates within a single generation ($-27\%$ to $-39\%$ by gen~1), reducing temporal resolution and making MAUVE pairs systematically undetectable (floor $\mu{=}0.029$).
With $T{\leq}25$ observations, statistical power remains limited: since $\alpha_\infty{\approx}0$, longer observation windows should push $\alpha_c$ toward arbitrarily low contamination levels, but sub-linear signal growth ($\hat{\beta}{=}0.66$, CI $[0.24, 0.78]$) means diminishing returns; two of five methods (threshold onset, Toda--Yamamoto) are power-limited at these series lengths.
The non-monotonic dip at $\alpha{=}0.60$ dissolves by $T{=}25$ but its mechanism---whether driven by numerical precision effects (bf16 yields 8/8), signal structure, or their interaction---remains open; boundary cells show substantial seed sensitivity (e.g., $T{=}10$, $\alpha{=}0.50$: 6/8, 0/8, 6/8 across three seeds).
All experiments use a single generation strategy (temperature~$1.0$, top-$k{=}50$); alternative decoding settings (nucleus sampling, lower temperature) may alter the collapse dynamics and detection landscape.
PermG's empirical FPR of $0/24$ yields a Clopper--Pearson 97.5\% upper bound of 14\%, but the three seeds are not independent (within-seed ICC${=}0.34$), widening the cluster-adjusted CI to $[0\%, 41\%]$; true FPR may be non-negligible.

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

When language models train iteratively on their own output, the training distribution progressively loses its tail modes, a phenomenon termed model collapse~\cite{shumailov2024curse,alemohammad2024mad}.
Lexical diversity narrows, calibration deteriorates, and each generation inherits the systematic biases of its predecessors.
As machine-generated text becomes prevalent on the web, such feedback loops pose a growing risk to production training pipelines.
By the time standard quality metrics register degradation, the underlying distribution may have already shifted irreversibly.

This threat motivates a fundamental question: \emph{what does the detectability landscape of model collapse look like?}
At what contamination level does statistical detection become possible, how does this boundary depend on observation length and statistical method, and what structure does the landscape exhibit?
Iterative training produces short, noisy time series (often fewer than 15 points per generation sequence), where detection power drops sharply~\cite{boettiger2012limits}, and existing analyses leave these dependencies unresolved.
Our detection mechanism (Granger temporal precedence) differs from critical-slowing-down indicators, as model collapse is a first-order transition~\cite{truong2026phase} (\S\ref{sec:related_work}).

We systematically map this landscape using Pythia-410M~\cite{biderman2023pythia} across 13 contamination levels (including null control) with multi-seed replication, applying five statistical methods from econometrics~\cite{granger1974spurious,toda1995statistical} to identical data.
The resulting map reveals structured terrain: blind zones where collapse proceeds undetected, a sharp onset where detection jumps from null to reliable within a 2-percentage-point interval, a non-monotonic dip where Granger detection fails despite confirmed causal flow, and a detection boundary $\alpha_c(T)$ that follows a power law in observation length.
Cross-architecture validation across five families (345M--6.9B) confirms the landscape generalizes when entropy-diversity coupling is preserved.
Granger precedence establishes temporal predictive improvement, not true causality~\cite{shojaie2022granger}; our canary claim is scoped to diversity metrics (distinct-$n$~\cite{li2016diversity}).

Our contributions are:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Detectability landscape characterization} (\S\ref{sec:regime}--\ref{sec:intervention}).
    PermG establishes a monotonically decreasing detection boundary $\alpha_c(T)$ following a power law in observation length (Proposition~\ref{prop:phase-boundary}), primarily characterized on Pythia-410M; leave-one-$T$-out CV confirms predictive accuracy (MAE${=}0.037$, CI~$15/15$; \S\ref{sec:theory}).
    Since $\alpha_\infty{\approx}0$, any nonzero contamination produces signal, but sub-linear growth makes detection a function of $T$.
    Predict-then-verify at $T{=}20$ matches 3/5 predictions in saturated regimes, with systematic conservative bias at boundary $\alpha$ (Appendix~\ref{app:t20_prediction_timeline}); canary-triggered cessation reduces peak perplexity by 58\%.

    \item \textbf{Formal motivation for canary metric selection} (\S\ref{sec:cascade}).
    Under mode amplification, entropy Granger-precedes diversity (Proposition~\ref{thm:entropy_leads}), with a ${\geq}1$-generation lag (Proposition~\ref{prop:div_lag}), confirmed in 14/15 experiments ($\alpha \geq 0.30$; GPT-2-medium s43 bidirectional).

    \item \textbf{Method sensitivity as a primary finding} (\S\ref{sec:mmct}--\ref{sec:dose_response}).
    Five detection methods yield null-control FPR from 0\% to 92\%; the same Granger test shifts from 0/8 to 6/8 within a 2-percentage-point interval.
    The detectability landscape one observes depends critically on the statistical method used to probe it.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.55\textwidth]{figures/fig_phase_diagram.pdf}
\caption{Detection phase diagram (Pythia-410M, fp32, PermG direction-checked). Each cell shows the number of FDR-significant canary$\to$diversity pairs (of~8) at a given contamination strength~$\alpha$ and observation window~$T$. The dashed curve is the theoretical detection boundary $\alpha_c(T) \propto T^{-\gamma}$ with $\gamma{=}2.08$, fitted (Proposition~\ref{prop:phase-boundary}). Diamond markers ($\diamond$) flag the synchronous dip at $\alpha{=}0.60$ (0/8 at $T{\leq}20$); the star ($\star$) marks its dissolution at $T{=}25$ (5/8), validating $\sqrt{T}$ power scaling. Dagger ($\dagger$): seed sensitivity at boundary ($T{=}10$, $\alpha{=}0.50$: s42${=}$6/8, s43${=}$0/8).}
\label{fig:regime_map}
\end{figure*}

19	Despite this ubiquitous degradation, Granger detectability is sharply regime-dependent.
20	The onset we report reflects PermG's statistical power curve crossing the detection threshold at a critical contamination level, not the emergence of a new physical signal; this interpretation is confirmed by sub-threshold $p$-values at $\alpha{=}0.45$ (\S\ref{sec:theory}).
21	Permutation Granger (PermG) tests find 0/8 canary$\to$downstream pairs FDR-significant from $\alpha{=}0.00$ through $\alpha{=}0.45$, then jump to 6/8 at $\alpha{=}0.50$ across all 3~fp32 seeds.
22	This transition is striking because cumulative synthetic fraction barely changes across the boundary: $C = 1{-}(1{-}\alpha)^{10}$ yields $99.75\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.45$ versus $99.90\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.50$, a difference of 0.15 percentage points, yet detection jumps from null to reliable.
23	Sigmoid regression on the 13-point $T{=}10$ grid yields $\alpha_c = 0.483 \pm 0.006$ ($R^2 = 0.969$); dense $\alpha$ sampling (17~values) constrains the onset steepness to $k{=}15.7$ (95\% CI $[9.4, 28.2]$), a steep but finite-width sigmoid (Figure~\ref{fig:regime_map}).
24	This single-$T$ estimate is consistent with the cross-$T$ validated model (\S\ref{sec:theory}), which predicts how the detection boundary shifts with observation length ($\gamma{=}2.08$).
25	The transition is not a literal step function ($\Delta\mathrm{AIC}{=}-110$ favoring sigmoid; Appendix~\ref{app:sigmoid_shape}), but its steepness (${\approx}3{\times}$ smooth-model predictions; \S\ref{sec:theory}) exceeds what PermG power curves alone produce.

Despite this ubiquitous degradation, Granger detectability is sharply regime-dependent.
The onset we report reflects PermG's statistical power curve crossing the detection threshold at a critical contamination level, not the emergence of a new physical signal; this interpretation is confirmed by sub-threshold $p$-values at $\alpha{=}0.45$ (\S\ref{sec:theory}).
Permutation Granger (PermG) tests find 0/8 canary$\to$downstream pairs FDR-significant from $\alpha{=}0.00$ through $\alpha{=}0.45$, then jump to 6/8 at $\alpha{=}0.50$ across all 3~fp32 seeds.
This transition is striking because cumulative synthetic fraction barely changes across the boundary: $C = 1{-}(1{-}\alpha)^{10}$ yields $99.75\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.45$ versus $99.90\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.50$, a difference of 0.15 percentage points, yet detection jumps from null to reliable.
Sigmoid regression on the 13-point $T{=}10$ grid yields $\alpha_c = 0.483 \pm 0.006$ ($R^2 = 0.969$); dense $\alpha$ sampling (17~values) constrains the onset steepness to $k{=}15.7$ (95\% CI $[9.4, 28.2]$), a steep but finite-width sigmoid (Figure~\ref{fig:regime_map}).
This single-$T$ estimate is consistent with the cross-$T$ validated model (\S\ref{sec:theory}), which predicts how the detection boundary shifts with observation length ($\gamma{=}2.08$).
The transition is not a literal step function ($\Delta\mathrm{AIC}{=}-110$ favoring sigmoid; Appendix~\ref{app:sigmoid_shape}), but its steepness (${\approx}3{\times}$ smooth-model predictions; \S\ref{sec:theory}) exceeds what PermG power curves alone produce.
At $T{=}10$, PermG power is ${\approx}37\%$ (Appendix~\ref{app:power_sim}), partly amplifying the $0/8{\to}6/8$ sharpness; however, onset steepness ($k{=}15.7$, ${\approx}3{\times}$ smooth predictions) and cross-seed consistency (3/3 seeds: $0/8{\to}6/8$ at $\alpha{=}0.48{\to}0.50$) argue for a genuine, power-modulated transition.
A Fisher exact test corroborates the categorical jump: 0/64 pairs FDR-significant at $\alpha \leq 0.45$ versus 18/32 at $\alpha \geq 0.50$ ($p = 3.45 \times 10^{-11}$); sub-threshold $p$-values at $\alpha{=}0.45$ ($p_{\mathrm{fdr}} = 0.059$--$0.091$) are consistent with proximity to the power boundary (\S\ref{sec:theory}).
A systematic robustness analysis (1{,}160 configurations) confirms specification-invariance of the onset.

1	\section{Discussion and Conclusion}\label{sec:discussion}
2	
3	\paragraph{Granger precedence is not causation.}
4	Our claim is scoped to temporal predictive improvement~\cite{granger1969investigating,shojaie2022granger}; bivariate tests cannot exclude confounders, and our cluster-adjusted FPR CI ($[0\%, 41\%]$; \S\ref{sec:limitations}) means true Type~I error may be non-negligible.
5	
6	\paragraph{Non-confirming cells.}
7	Five of twenty phase-diagram cells show $0/8$ despite lying above the theoretical detection boundary: four are sync-dip cells ($\alpha{=}0.60$, $T{=}10$--$20$) and one is a boundary cell ($T{=}10$, $\alpha{=}0.45$).
8	The sync-dip dissolves by $T{=}25$ ($5/8$), confirming it is transient; its mechanism remains open---one hypothesis is synchronization between the replacement ratio and the model's internal mode dynamics.
9	Excluding these five cells, the remaining 15/15 match theory (LOO-CV MAE${=}0.037$).
10	
11	\paragraph{Metric-specific ceiling.}
12	Observed detection counts never exceed $6/8$: the 2/8 non-detected pairs involve MAUVE, whose floor saturation ($\mu{=}0.029$) eliminates the temporal gradient Granger precedence requires (\S\ref{sec:t20}); practitioners should prefer monotonically degrading metrics (e.g., distinct-$n$).
13	
14	\paragraph{Cross-architecture failure modes.}
15	Five of fifteen conditions do not confirm forward detection (\S\ref{sec:generalization}): precision sensitivity (GPT-2 bf16: 0/8 vs fp32 6/8), bidirectional confounding (GPT-2 s43: reverse 6/8), seed dependence (Pythia-1.4B: s42 2/8 vs s43 6/8), and architecture-specific decoupling (SmolLM3-3B entropy 0/4, violating mode amplification; Proposition~\ref{thm:entropy_leads}).
16	Phase-diagram replication at 1.4B confirms qualitatively preserved detection despite count attenuation (4--5/8; Appendix~\ref{app:scale_14b}).
17	
18	\paragraph{Entropy-diversity coupling.}
19	The entropy-diversity lag is structural: distinct-$n$ requires token mass to cross threshold~$\varepsilon$ ($\gamma$-margin; Proposition~\ref{prop:div_lag}), producing the ${\geq}1$-generation lag in 14/15 experiments; PermG's directional asymmetry (6/8 forward, 0/8 reverse) argues against a sensitivity artifact.
20	
21	\paragraph{Domain-dependent directionality.}
22	WikiText yields exclusively forward PermG significance; C4 produces reverse 7/8 at $\alpha{=}0.50$ (Appendix~\ref{app:extended_discussion}), indicating domain-dependent confounding.
23	
24	\paragraph{Practical implications.}
25	Longer $T$ lowers $\alpha_c$ sub-linearly (\S\ref{sec:theory}); PermG requires fp32 (bf16: 0/8 vs 6/8 in GPT-2).
26	Entropy is the optimal canary (14/15 cascade); triggered cessation reduces peak perplexity by 58\% (\S\ref{sec:intervention}), bridging the detection-to-action gap that prior work leaves open.

lines: Diversity collapse occurs at every contamination level: distinct-1 declines by $14.1\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.0$ (fine-tuning drift) and by $40.3{\pm}0.3\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.25$ (3-seed mean).
Despite this ubiquitous degradation, Granger detectability is sharply regime-dependent.

The onset we report reflects PermG's statistical power curve crossing the detection threshold at a critical contamination level, not the emergence of a new physical signal; this interpretation is confirmed by sub-threshold $p$-values at $\alpha{=}0.45$ (\S\ref{sec:theory}).

-Permutation Granger (PermG) tests find 0/8 canary$\to$downstream pairs FDR-significant from $\alpha{=}0.00$ through $\alpha{=}0.45$, then jump to 6/8 at $\alpha{=}0.50$ across all 3~fp32 seeds, indicating robust detection with no significant seed variance at this critical transition.

+Permutation Granger (PermG) tests find 0/8 canary$\to$downstream pairs FDR-significant from $\alpha{=}0.00$ through $\alpha{=}0.45$, then jump to 6/8 at $\alpha{=}0.50$ uniformly across all 3~fp32 seeds.

This transition is striking because cumulative synthetic fraction barely changes across the boundary: $C = 1{-}(1{-}\alpha)^{10}$ yields $99.75\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.45$ versus $99.90\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.50$, a difference of 0.15 percentage points, yet detection jumps from null to reliable.

Sigmoid regression on the 13-point $T{=}10$ grid yields $\alpha_c = 0.483 \pm 0.006$ ($R^2 = 0.969$); dense $\alpha$ sampling (17~values) constrains the onset steepness to $k{=}15.7$ (95\% CI $[9.4, 28.2]$), a steep but finite-width sigmoid (Figure~\ref{fig:regime_map}).
This single-$T$ estimate is consistent with the cross-$T$ validated model (\S\ref{sec:theory}), which predicts how the detection boundary shifts with observation length ($\gamma{=}2.08$).

1	\section{Discussion and Conclusion}\label{sec:discussion}
2	
3	\paragraph{Granger precedence is not causation.}
4	Our claim is scoped to temporal predictive improvement~\cite{granger1969investigating,shojaie2022granger}; bivariate tests cannot exclude confounders, and our cluster-adjusted FPR CI ($[0\%, 41\%]$; \S\ref{sec:limitations}) means true Type~I error may be non-negligible.
5	
6	\paragraph{Non-confirming cells.}
7	Five of twenty phase-diagram cells show $0/8$ despite lying above the theoretical detection boundary: four are sync-dip cells ($\alpha{=}0.60$, $T{=}10$--$20$) and one is a boundary cell ($T{=}10$, $\alpha{=}0.45$).
8	The sync-dip dissolves by $T{=}25$ ($5/8$), confirming it is transient; its mechanism remains open---one hypothesis is synchronization between the replacement ratio and the model's internal mode dynamics.
9	Excluding these five cells, the remaining 15/15 match theory (LOO-CV MAE${=}0.037$).
10	
11	\paragraph{Metric-specific ceiling.}
12	Observed detection counts never exceed $6/8$: the 2/8 non-detected pairs involve MAUVE, whose floor saturation ($\mu{=}0.029$) eliminates the temporal gradient Granger precedence requires (\S\ref{sec:t20}); practitioners should prefer monotonically degrading metrics (e.g., distinct-$n$).
13	
14	\paragraph{Cross-architecture failure modes.}
15	Five of fifteen conditions do not confirm forward detection (\S\ref{sec:generalization}): precision sensitivity (GPT-2 bf16: 0/8 vs fp32 6/8), bidirectional confounding (GPT-2 s43: reverse 6/8), seed dependence (Pythia-1.4B: s42 2/8 vs s43 6/8), and architecture-specific decoupling (SmolLM3-3B entropy 0/4, violating mode amplification; Proposition~\ref{thm:entropy_leads}).
16	Phase-diagram replication at 1.4B confirms qualitatively preserved detection despite count attenuation (4--5/8; Appendix~\ref{app:scale_14b}).
17	
18	\paragraph{Entropy-diversity coupling.}
19	The entropy-diversity lag is structural: distinct-$n$ requires token mass to cross threshold~$\varepsilon$ ($\gamma$-margin; Proposition~\ref{prop:div_lag}), producing the ${\geq}1$-generation lag in 14/15 experiments; PermG's directional asymmetry (6/8 forward, 0/8 reverse) argues against a sensitivity artifact.
20	However, directionality is domain-dependent: WikiText yields exclusively forward significance, while C4 produces reverse 7/8 at $\alpha{=}0.50$ (Appendix~\ref{app:extended_discussion}).
21	
22	\paragraph{Practical implications.}
23	Longer $T$ lowers $\alpha_c$ sub-linearly (\S\ref{sec:theory}); PermG requires fp32 (bf16: 0/8 vs 6/8 in GPT-2).
24	Triggered cessation on entropy (optimal canary; 14/15 cascade) reduces peak perplexity by 58\% (\S\ref{sec:intervention}), bridging detection to action.

\section{Discussion and Conclusion}\label{sec:discussion}

\paragraph{Granger precedence is not causation.}
Our claim is scoped to temporal predictive improvement~\cite{granger1969investigating,shojaie2022granger}; bivariate tests cannot exclude confounders, and our cluster-adjusted FPR CI ($[0\%, 41\%]$; \S\ref{sec:limitations}) means true Type~I error may be non-negligible.

\paragraph{Non-confirming cells.}
Five of twenty phase-diagram cells show $0/8$ despite lying above the theoretical detection boundary: four are sync-dip cells ($\alpha{=}0.60$, $T{=}10$--$20$) and one is a boundary cell ($T{=}10$, $\alpha{=}0.45$).
The sync-dip dissolves by $T{=}25$ ($5/8$), confirming it is transient; its mechanism remains open.
Excluding these five cells, the remaining 15/15 match theory (LOO-CV MAE${=}0.037$).

\paragraph{Metric-specific ceiling.}
Observed detection counts never exceed $6/8$: the 2/8 non-detected pairs involve MAUVE, whose floor saturation ($\mu{=}0.029$) eliminates the temporal gradient Granger precedence requires (\S\ref{sec:t20}); practitioners should prefer monotonically degrading metrics (e.g., distinct-$n$).

\paragraph{Cross-architecture failure modes.}
Five of fifteen conditions do not confirm forward detection (\S\ref{sec:generalization}): precision sensitivity (GPT-2 bf16: 0/8 vs fp32 6/8), bidirectional confounding (GPT-2 s43: reverse 6/8), seed dependence (Pythia-1.4B: s42 2/8 vs s43 6/8), and architecture-specific decoupling (SmolLM3-3B entropy 0/4).
Phase-diagram replication at 1.4B confirms qualitatively preserved detection despite count attenuation (4--5/8; Appendix~\ref{app:scale_14b}).

\paragraph{Entropy-diversity coupling.}
The entropy-diversity lag is structural: distinct-$n$ requires token mass to cross threshold~$\varepsilon$ ($\gamma$-margin; Proposition~\ref{prop:div_lag}), producing the ${\geq}1$-generation lag in 14/15 experiments; PermG's directional asymmetry (6/8 forward, 0/8 reverse) argues against a sensitivity artifact.
However, directionality is domain-dependent: WikiText yields exclusively forward significance, while C4 produces reverse 7/8 at $\alpha{=}0.50$ (Appendix~\ref{app:extended_discussion}).

\paragraph{Practical implications.}
Longer $T$ lowers $\alpha_c$ sub-linearly (\S\ref{sec:theory}); PermG requires fp32 (bf16: 0/8 vs 6/8 in GPT-2).
Triggered cessation on entropy (optimal canary; 14/15 cascade) reduces peak perplexity by 58\% (\S\ref{sec:intervention}), bridging detection to action.
